title: Stock Market Live, Aug 17: Sensex down 280 pts as markets close, Nifty down 80 pts to 24,287.65; Infosys, HCL Tech are top losers - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live updates - Sensex and Nifty opened lower, Nifty at 24,343.45 and Sensex at 77,892.92, before sliding further in early trade.

Brent crude held near $88.6 a barrel, having risen 5% last week, keeping pressure on India as an import-dependent economy.

The rupee was hovering near 95.6 against the dollar, adding to the strain. GIFT Nifty had signalled a muted start, pointing to around 24,407 before the open.

Among Nifty 50 stocks, metals saw mixed action. Hindalco was the top gainer, up 1.17% to ₹1,041.50, while JSW Steel was the biggest loser, falling 1.36% to ₹1,252.70. The metal sector as a whole shed 1.8% over last week.

On the losing side, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories fell 1.09% to ₹1,186.90, State Bank of India dropped 0.99% to ₹1,057.10, TCS declined 0.94% to ₹2,338.70, and Jio Financial Services slipped 0.92% to ₹246.75.

On the occasion of India’s 80th Independence Day, Bank of India (New Zealand) Ltd launched its new mobile banking application, “BOINZ - Freedom”, at a special gathering hosted in Auckland in the presence of around 500 guests. The application was formally inaugurated by the Consul General of India, Auckland, marking a significant milestone in Bank of India’s journey of strengthening its digital banking presence in New Zealand.

The MD & CEO of the parent bank, Bank of India, Shri Rajneesh Karnatak, addressed the gathering through a video message. The first overseas branch of Bank of India was opened in London, United Kingdom, in 1946. At present, Bank of India has a presence in 15 countries, namely the US, Cayman Islands, United Kingdom, France, Belgium, Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Zambia, UAE, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam, New Zealand and Japan, spanning five continents.

Bank of India has had a presence in New Zealand since 2011 through its wholly owned subsidiary, BOI(NZ)L, with two branches at Auckland and Papatoetoe.

API Holdings, India’s largest digital healthcare platform and the ultimate parent company of Thyrocare, has become debt-free after repaying its outstanding debt of ₹1,050 crore. The repayment was funded through proceeds from the recent sale of a portion of its stake in Thyrocare Technologies and internal accruals.

Docon Technologies Private Ltd, the promoter and holding company of Thyrocare, sold 1,57,69,696 Thyrocare shares, representing around 9.90 per cent of the company’s paid-up equity share capital, through market trades. Following the sale, Docon continues to remain the promoter and holding company of Thyrocare with a 51.02 per cent stake.

The debt repayment has also resulted in the release of the pledge on the remaining Thyrocare shares held by Docon. The entire outstanding pledge linked to the debt has now been released, leaving Docon’s 51.02 per cent holding in Thyrocare fully unencumbered.

Alok Kumar Jagnani, Whole-Time Director and Group CFO, API Holdings, said, “We’ve repaid our term debt in full, and we did it the hard way, without diluting our stake in Thyrocare below 51 per cent. That’s the real headline: a stronger balance sheet without giving up our ownership. It reflects a capital allocation philosophy where growth and discipline aren’t traded off against each other. With every business in the group soon profitable, there’s no drag left on the P&L; just a clean base to build from.”

Siddharth Shah, Vice Chairman, API Holdings, said, “The Thyrocare acquisition has worked out well for API. Shareholders who held on instead of tendering to our open offer at ₹433 a share in July 2021 (bonus adjusted) are sitting on ₹653 at close of trading on 14 August 2026 — dividends included. That’s a 51 per cent return. NIFTY 50 gave you 41 per cent. Pathology peers weren’t even close. True value for money! Congratulations to the Thyrocare team, a turnaround nobody thought was possible.”

Rahul Guha, MD & CEO, API Holdings and Thyrocare, said, “Zero debt isn’t the finish line; it’s the starting gun. This wasn’t financial engineering; it was Thyrocare’s and the group’s execution, quarter after quarter, that made it possible. What the team proved is bigger than a balance sheet: this organisation can execute on anything it sets its mind to. That’s the real asset we’re carrying into the next chapter.”

With its term loan fully repaid and businesses moving into profitability, API Holdings now enters its next phase focused on profitable growth, disciplined execution and long-term value creation across its healthcare businesses.

Shilp Gravures Ltd’s board has approved the proposed capacity expansion for the purchase of plant and machinery and to set up manufacturing facilities in Karnataka.

Goodluck India’s board has approved August 21, 2026, as the record date for determining the eligibility of shareholders entitled to the issuance and allotment of bonus equity shares in the ratio of 2:1.

Cognizant launches a Talent Accelerator programme for 489 B-school graduates, fostering collaboration and bridging AI with business outcomes.

CG Power and Industrial Solutions’ wholly owned subsidiary, Axiro Semiconductor Private Ltd, has entered into a definitive agreement, i.e., a Securities Purchase Agreement, for the acquisition of 100 per cent of the shareholding in Tosil Systems Private Ltd (“Tosil”) for a consideration of ₹16.44 crore.

Gulshan Polyols has received an additional allocation of 20,740 kilolitres of ethanol for supply to Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) for Q4 of Ethanol Supply Year (ESY 2025-26) in the states of Assam and Madhya Pradesh. The estimated order value is ₹146 crore.

ADF Foods traded flat at ₹263 on the NSE, hitting a low of ₹258.90. Ascot appealed a US court ruling against the company’s arm; no stay was granted on the injunction or monetary judgment.

Hindustan Aeronautics traded flat at Rs 5,062.80 on the NSE at 2.43 pm after hitting a fresh 52-week high of Rs 5,149.90 following a pact with Adani Defence and BEML for manufacturing fuselage structures for Light Combat Helicopters
